name: Lennon Adair
life: “I still remember a customer naming a seedling before it had roots.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Lennon takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I gave it the name of my favorite aunt. My other aunt just found out and wants a pot of her own.
appearance: Lennon has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Lennon touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Lennon keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Lennon wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To give the second aunt a cutting to name.
family: Micah Hassan is Lennon’s stepsibling. Lennon puts the kettle on. Micah chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The last light at the harbor*, Micah says, “I run the marina. I didn't understand how many people check on each other without passing through my office.”
connections: Elaine Marquez. One inherited name and one new cutting go to rooms where the plant can be welcomed. Also in the story is Talia Drew (plant stand maker).

reactions.situation: A patient asks to be alone with the plant
reactions.response: Lennon leaves the patient with the plant and returns at an agreed time.
